meetings.headline: Committee unanimously recommends the town not exercise right of first refusal on a 222 West Towns Road parcel
meetings.summary: The Open Space Committee welcomed two new members (from the Parks Commission and Planning Board), approved minutes from a prior joint meeting, and unanimously voted to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 13-acre Chapter 61 parcel at 222 West Towns Road, finding it did not meet the committee's open-space criteria. The committee also noted its open space plan was extended by the state to 2029, took on a homework assignment from the town's master-plan steering committee, and rescheduled its next meeting to September 3rd.

budget_items.topic: Open space plan extension / grant eligibility
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported the state approved extending the open space plan from a seven-year to a 10-year plan, valid through fiscal year 2029, which lets the committee keep applying for open space grants through June 2029 without redoing a plan update next year.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 61/61A/61B tax status on 222 West Towns Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair explained that landowners in chapter 61 (forestry), 61A (agriculture) or 61B (conservation/recreation) get a lower tax rate, and if they sell for development they exit chapter status, pay back taxes, and the town gets a right of first refusal to match a sale price.

meetings.headline: Longtime Open Space Committee member Brandon announced his resignation, effective immediately
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Open Space Committee met by Zoom; longtime member Brandon announced his resignation effective immediately, and the parks commission's representative Tim Lawless is also stepping down, leaving several vacancies. The committee approved February's minutes, discussed pursuing a three-year extension of the open space plan (to 2029) by updating its action-item table for state approval, and discussed tightening the six criteria used to evaluate right-of-first-refusal properties before adjourning.

decisions.decision: Brandon announced he is resigning from the Open Space Committee effective after this meeting and will send a resignation letter to the planning board (the committee's oversight board).
Tim Lawless, the parks commission's representative to the committee, is also stepping aside, creating another vacancy.
Committee will look at moving its June meeting to Monday, June 9th to coincide with the planning board's meeting, pending quorum.
Chair (Mike) will take the lead on updating the open space plan's action-item table from a 7-year to a 10-year format to secure a 3-year extension (to 2029) from the state.
Before sending the updated plan to the state, it will be circulated to the planning board, parks commission, agricultural commission, conservation commission, town manager and select board for input.
July meeting will remain on its usual date, the second Wednesday of July.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee tabled the request to list Farmland of Local Importance until its next monthly meeting, with no action requested yet.
The committee tabled a Chapter 61 right-of-first-refusal parcel on Townsend Harbor Road and made no recommendation, as members saw it as not meeting criteria.
A member is to raise streamlining notification of such parcels at the planning board, and the chair is to check the conservation commission's view.
The September minutes were approved by roll call once a quorum was regained after missing October through December.
The next meetings were set for February 12 and March 12 at 7:30 on Zoom, with in-person meetings to be considered from April.

why_it_matters: A Chapter 61 parcel gives the town a short window to use its right of first refusal, so tabling a case and the notification problems discussed can affect whether farmland or open land is considered in time.
No money was voted on; Town Hall design funding and a Conservation Commission state award came up only as comments, and no figures were given.
watch_next: The February 12 meeting at 7:30 on Zoom, where the tabled farmland request and the Townsend Harbor Road parcel may return.
The March 12 meeting, and whether in-person meetings resume from April.
